picks.title: 대만서도 'AI 대량 책 매입' 논란…"문화부, 출판산업 영향 파악해야"
picks.excerpt: 앤트로픽이 대만 도서유통사 연합발행(UDC)에서 2024년 11월부터 올해 9월까지 563톤의 책을 사들인 사실이 알려지며 대만 입법원에서 문화부 장관에게 출판산업 영향 파악을 요구하는 등 논란이 정치권으로 번지고 있다.
picks.rationale: New concrete event: Anthropic's 563-ton bulk book purchase in Taiwan reaches the legislature — a new market in the training-data book-buying story, not a rehash of the UK bookshop or Korean piracy cards.

picks.title: Copyright agreements allow use of content for AI prompts
picks.excerpt: New Zealand's Tāwhia Copyright Aotearoa (formerly Copyright Licensing New Zealand) has signed a bilateral agreement with the UK's Copyright Licensing Agency that lets licensed content be used in AI prompts.
picks.rationale: Concrete licensing deal (NZ Tāwhia x UK CLA) that makes AI-prompt use of licensed text a collective-licence right — directly actionable for publishers and rights holders.

picks.title: Polish lektor wins first AI voice deepfake ruling
picks.excerpt: A Warsaw court ruled on 13 November that adverts using an AI copy of film reader Jarosław Łukomski's voice were a deepfake, ordering removal, apologies and damages. In Poland's first cloned-voice trial, the judge said the protection covers anyone's voice, not only famous ones — a precedent for narrators and audiobook voices.
picks.rationale: First court ruling in Poland on a cloned voice, extending protection to any voice — a precedent narrators and audiobook producers can cite.

picks.title: Kakao, OpenAI Collaborate on AI-Generated Short Animation Based on Ryan Begins Webtoon
picks.excerpt: Kakao and OpenAI released an AI-generated short animation adapted from the Ryan Begins webtoon; the production team said it used roughly 1,500 prompts for a single scene to reach the intended direction and emotional tone.
picks.rationale: New release: a Kakao x OpenAI webtoon-to-animation short with a concrete production detail (about 1,500 prompts per scene) — distinct from the CreateCrew tooling card of 11-08.

picks.title: Around the Book World: Monday, November 9, 2026 (Robert Laffont vs Gallimard on AI manuscript screening)
picks.excerpt: Robert Laffont's managing director Frédéric Martin opposes using AI-detection software to screen submissions, saying author-publisher relations should rest on trust — while Gallimard parent Madrigall plans to screen manuscripts for AI.
picks.rationale: New policy split among French publishers: Madrigall (Gallimard) will screen submissions for AI while Robert Laffont refuses — changes what authors submitting in France can expect.
